title: OLNEY MURDER ARREST
full_story:
Dylan M. Jones, 25 of Olney was jailed in connection with a double homicide in Olney.  Jones was booked into the Richland County jail at Olney Tuesday night at 11:34 pm.

The dead were identified as John D. Jones, Jr, 52 and Deborah J. Jones, 73 of Olney.  Officers responded to two homes in the 400 block of East Monroe Street in Olney at 3:11 pm Tuesday afternoon and found the victims in separate houses.

title: CLAY COUNTY FAIR SCHEDULE
full_story:
The Clay County Fair will start Friday, July 24th at 4 pm with the 4H BBQ at the REA building.  Menu is a Salt & Strings pork chop, green beans, cheesy potatoes, homemade desert and drink for $12, or $5 for a hot dog meal.  You can pre-purchase tickets from Clay County 4-H members, or you can stop by the extension office at 210 S Church St., Louisville.

Gates will then open at 5:30 for the Crain Scates Bucking Bulls Rodeo hosted by the Clay County Farm Bureau Young Leaders.  Cost to enter the rodeo is $15, those 5 and under get in for free, pre show tickets are available from Young Leaders and are $12.  Mutton busting will be available for $10 with only 30 spots available for children under 80 lbs.

Saturday morning July 25th starts at 8 am with the poultry and rabbit check in.  The poultry show is at 9 am followed by the 4H and JR Rabbit Show.  All livestock should be on the fairgrounds by 3 pm.  There will also be a mandatory meeting for all livestock exhibitors and vet papers check at 3 pm.  After the meeting livestock weigh in will begin, and the night ends at 7 pm with the open sheep show.

Sunday, July 26th will have the JR Sheep show at 11 am and JR Goat show at Noon.  Registration for the kids pedal tractor pull at 1 pm next to the Merchants building, and the kids pull is at 2 pm, hosted by the Clay County Farm Bureau Young Leaders.  The 4H Horse show and JR Horse show is at 2 pm.  The Clay County Ministerial Alliance program is from 5:30 to 7 pm and there will be a greased pig contest at 7 pm sponsored by UPI Fairfield.

On Monday, July 27th the fair will kick into high gear with the 4H Beef Show at 8 am followed by the JR Beef Show, AITC Activities will be in the Farm Bureau building from 2 to 4 pm.  Then at 5 pm it’s the Mini Livestock Show for those 4 to 8 years of age hosted by the Clay County Farm Bureau Young Leaders.  The night ends with the Little Miss Pageant at 7:30 pm admission is $10 for adults and $5 for kids 3 – 10.  There are 19 young ladies vying for the title held by Izzabella Brinkley.

Tuesday will be Nutrien Ag Solutions Day at the fair with giveaways and activities throughout the day.  At 8 am is the 4H Swine show and Open Beef Show, followed by the Sheep Show at 1 pm and the 4H Goat Show at 2:30 pm.  Then at 5 pm will be the Master Showmanship Contest, sponsored by the Clay County Farm Bureau Young Leaders.  On the stage at 7:30 pm will be the Junior Miss Clay County Fair Pageant and Queen pie auction.  Admission to the Junior Miss pageant is $10 for adults and $5 for kids 3 – 10.  There are 10 contestants, Halle Patridge is the current JR Miss.

Wednesday will start at 8 am with the JR Swine Show followed by the Open Goat Show.  DaS zle Dance and Tumble will perform at 5 pm, admission is free, and the 4H Livestock Auction will begin at 6:30pm.

Thursday opens at 8 am with the Open Dairy Show, then at 5 pm Joni’s Power & Grace Tumbling will be in the REA building, admission is free.  The Lickity Split and Legally Sheila concert will be on the stage 7 pm.

The Fair will culminate with the Clay County Fair Queen Pageant Friday night, July 31st at 7 pm, with admission $10 for adults and $5 for kids 3 – 10.  There are 13 young ladies vying for the title.  The current Queen is Olivia Haun.

title: BACK TO SCHOOL VACCINE CLINICS
full_story:
The Clay County Health Department is having a series of Back-to-School vaccine clinics.

The next clinic will be on Friday, July 17th from 8:30 am to 5 pm at the Health Department on 12th Street.  Appointments are not necessary but are appreciated.  Appointments can be made by calling 618-662-4406.

Illinois state law requires certain immunizations for children and adults enrolled in childcare, school, or college.  State law also mandates immunizations for adults in specific fields of work.

There will also be Back-to-School vaccine clinics on Thursday, July 23rd from 8:30 am to 5 pm; on August 3rd, 6th, 12th, and 13th from 8:30 am to 6 pm.  The final clinic will be from Friday, August 14th from 8 am to Noon.

Again appointments are not necessary, but appreciated, if you have questions call the Clay County Health Department at 618-662-4406.

title: SBDC PROGRAMS ON BUSINESS
full_story:
The SBDC at IECC is presenting a lender Forum on July 14th from 9 to Noon in the OCC Banquet Room.

Presenters will include SBA staff, 504 corporations, SBDC representatives, Illinois Advantage Representatives, the state Treasurers Office, and microlenders.  Topics will include SOP Changes, updated lender match info, and upcoming SBA initiatives and training opportunities.

Then from 1 to 3 pm the SBDC at IECC will present a session on Funding opportunities for Businesses in the same room.

Speakers will include Mark Lambird talking about TIF and Enterprise Zone Fund, The Greater Wabash Regional Planning Commission, Advantage Illinois, the SBA and Trustbank.

For more information or to sign up for the Workshop call Michelle Brooks at 618-562-3744 or visit the iecc.edu/sbdc.

The programs are funded in part through a cooperative agreement with the US SBA, the Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity and the Illinois Eastern Community College.

title: VALENTINE TRIAL MOVED
full_story:
The trial for a southern Illinois woman accused of killing her husband will be moved from Edwards County to Williamson County.

The motion for a change of venue, was granted Tuesday.  Authorities allege Megan Valentine shot her husband, Judge Michael Valentine, at their home in Albion.

Michael served as the county’s judge since 2016 and as the state attorney for eight years before that.

Valentine’s trial will be held in Williamson County.  With her next court date is set in September.

title: INTRODUCTION TO NURSING
full_story:
Lake Land College is hosting an Introduction to Nursing event for high school students on Tuesday, July 14th from 10 am to 4 pm in Neal Hall room 101.  The event is designed for students interested in the nursing profession to learn about the programs and resources available at Lake Land College as well as the career opportunities available in the field.

During the event, students in attendance will meet with faculty and staff, tour Lake Land’s nursing facilities and develop their skills in a variety of hands-on activities.  They will also enjoy the opportunity to experience and practice realistic patient care in the College’s high-fidelity patient simulation lab.  Additionally, attendees will learn everything they need to know about the nursing program admission process, from financial aid options to tips for the entrance exam.  A free pizza lunch will also be provided for all students in attendance.

Space for the Introduction to Nursing event is limited to the first 30 registrants.  Registration is available online.

The Lake Land College Introduction to Nursing Event is offered with sponsorship support from St. Anthony’s Memorial Hospital and Good Shepard Hospital.

To learn more about the Lake Land College Introduction to Nursing Event, contact Nursing Instructor Nichole Jones at 217-234-5455 or [email protected].

title: LIHEAP AVAILABLE
full_story:
CEFS Economic Opportunity Corporation’s Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) still has funding available.  Applications for the current program year will be accepted through August 14th.

Households that applied on or after October 1st, may only reapply if facing utility disconnection.  Those who previously received reconnection assistance should contact their local CEFS Outreach Office to check eligibility for additional help.

Since October 1st, CEFS has approved $537,216.00 in energy benefits for 716 Clay County households, averaging $750 per household.  An additional 229 households received $168,613 in emergency reconnection assistance, averaging $736.

Monthly Income Eligibility are as follows: 1 person can make up to $3,332 per month, 2 people can make up to $4,357 a month, 3 people can make up to $5,382, and 4 people can make up to $6,407 per month.  Income limits for larger households are available at www.cefseoc.org or www.liheapillinois.com.

To schedule an appointment, contact the CEFS Clay County Outreach Office at 618-662-4024 which is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 am – 4:30 pm, or schedule online at www.cefseoc.org.  Applications can be completed in person or by phone, and documents may be submitted in person, by mail, or electronically.  Those needing any special accommodation should contact their local CEFS office.

LIHEAP is funded by the US Department of Health and Human Services and the Illinois Department of Commerce & Economic Opportunity.  CEFS administers the program in Clay, Christian, Effingham, Fayette, Montgomery, Moultrie, and Shelby counties.

title: MEGA MILLIONS
full_story:
After no Mega Millions ticket matched all six numbers drawn Tuesday night the estimated jackpot for Friday, is $604 million or $266.3 million cash.

While the jackpot remains elusive, the number of winning tickets at all other prize levels keeps increasing, there were a total of 368,067 winning tickets for the July 7th drawing.  The biggest winners were six tickets, that matched 4 numbers and the Mega Ball for prizes ranging from $20,000 to $100,000.

The jackpot has been growing since it was last won at $60 million on March 17th in Van Wert, Ohio.

Only two Mega Millions jackpots have been won so far this year.

Half of the proceeds from the sale of each Mega Millions ticket remains in the state where the ticket was sold, where the money supports designated good causes and retailer commissions.

Drawings are conducted at 11 pm Eastern on Tuesdays and Fridays in Atlanta, Georgia.

title: FFA 100 YEARS BOOK
full_story:
To coincide with the 100th Illinois FFA Convention in two years, a book will be released documenting the history.  Retired ag teacher Jeff Maierhofer (myer-hoffer) is helping with the project.

The 100th Illinois FFA Convention will be held in 2028 at the Peoria Civic Center.

Maierhofer spent 34 years as the FFA Advisor at Seneca High School.  He serves on the Illinois FFA 100th Celebration Committee.
